note: Trimmed extract of the Lighthouse run against the standalone production server (NEXT_OUTPUT_STANDALONE build served by node .next/standalone/server.js, with .next/static and public staged as the Dockerfile does), / at 1440x900, default mobile-throttled preset. The full report is ~584 KB of trace payload; the raw file is gitignored and only the figures the audit cites are kept here. Chromium-only and machine-specific: order-of-magnitude, not a Core Web Vitals guarantee.
provenance: This is the run taken AFTER fixing the two defects it originally surfaced (A11Y-010 button-name, A11Y-011 heading-order), which is why accessibility reads 100 and those audits score 1. The earlier run that exposed them recorded accessibility 93 with button-name and heading-order both 0; its raw output was not retained, so that figure is cited from the session record and not from a file in this directory.
